title: fix(plugin-detail): feed diagnostics name the block that carries the bad value, dedupe per block
body:
Fixes #9557
Clause-②: no

## What changed

The shared feed pipeline `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordActivityFeed.ts` is run by three blocks: `record:activity` (members on its own node) and `record:chatter` / `record:discussion` (members on their nested `feed`). Its author diagnostics for an unrecognised `filterMode`, an unrecognised `types` entry, a non-array `types`, and a `types` kind nothing produces were hard-prefixed `[record:activity]` and deduped on the offending value alone.

- `normalizeFilterMode`, `normalizeFeedTypes` and `applyFeedConfig` now take the calling block's name as a **required** last argument (no default, so no caller can inherit another block's name). These three are exported from the module but not from the package barrel; the only callers outside tests are `record-activity.tsx` and `record-chatter.tsx`.
- `warnOnce` takes a `scope`; the four authored-value channels pass the block name, so the message is prefixed with it and the warn-once key is the (block, value) pair (joined with `JSON.stringify`, so no two pairs can collide by concatenation).
- `record-activity.tsx` passes `record:activity` (one module constant, also used for its existing row-cap message). `record-chatter.tsx` passes the block it is mounted as (`schema.type`, which is `record:chatter` or `record:discussion`). It falls back to `record:chatter` only when no type arrives: the host's auto-appended discussion mounts the renderer with no schema, and then its `feed` holds only the three affordance defaults, which none of these diagnostics reads. The existing row-cap message already used the same expression; it is now computed once and shared.
- Nothing that renders changes. The `sys_activity` row-type warning keeps its prefix and stays unscoped: it reports a value in the data, not a member an author wrote on a block (see Acceptance notes).

## Tests (head `5fca701`)

New pin `renderers/__tests__/recordFeedDiagnosticBlockName-9557.test.tsx`, 7 cases:
- ONE-PER-BLOCK: the same bad `filterMode` through `record:activity` and `record:chatter` warns twice, under each name. This is checked on the pure half and again with both blocks mounted through `SchemaRenderer` on one page, so the name comes from the real node `type`. The same holds for an unrecognised `types` entry (`record:activity` + `record:discussion`), a non-array `types`, and an unproduced kind.
- STILL-ONCE (control): the same block with the same value warns once, whether it is re-run or re-mounted.
- NO-FOREIGN-NAME: bad `feed.filterMode` + `feed.types` on `record:discussion` are reported under `[record:discussion]` and never contain `[record:activity]`.

Existing call sites in `recordActivityFeed.test.ts`, `recordActivityFeed.rowLimitRefusal-10096.test.tsx`, `spec-symbol-batch7.test.ts` (block `record:activity`) and the row oracle in `recordChatterFeedMembersLive-8934.test.tsx` gained the argument. PM hypothesis 3 did not hold: no existing pin asserts the `[record:activity]` literal on a chatter path, so there was no pin to rewrite.

Runs (root-form vitest, through the shared verify lock):
- `vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` at `c6e7e1c`: `Test Files 202 passed | 1 skipped (203)`, `Tests 2046 passed | 8 skipped (2054)`. `5fca701` changes only a changeset and two casts in the new test.
- 6 related files at `5fca701`: `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 157 passed (157)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exit 0 at `5fca701`, after building the dependency closure. `--listFiles` on the test project names all five edited test files and the new one.

Ablations (committed tree, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from the objectstack checkout, restore proven by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`):
1. Dedupe back to value-only (`JSON.stringify([scope, k])` replaced by `String(k)`, 2 hits): **4 failed / 3 passed**. The four ONE-PER-BLOCK cases went red. Both STILL-ONCE controls and NO-FOREIGN-NAME stayed green, as they should. The first try used the replacement `k`, and the tool refused it before running anything because `k` already occurs 293 times, so the count could not rise. That try was a no-op and is not counted.
2. `filterMode` prefix hard-coded back to `[record:activity]` (1 hit): **3 failed / 4 passed**. Red: the pure filterMode ONE-PER-BLOCK case, the rendered ONE-PER-BLOCK case and NO-FOREIGN-NAME.

## Gates (objectui, derived by hand from `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` for the touched files)

All exit 0 at `5fca701`: `check-changeset-presence` (1 released package, 1 changeset), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`. Earlier at the same content: `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:shell-escape-residue`.
ESLint, narrowed and **not** the repo-wide `pnpm lint`: `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 8 touched TS files gave 0 errors and 38 warnings (all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` / `set-state-in-effect`; the new test has 0). Repo-wide lint is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- The card says six hard-coded prefixes. On `origin/main` there are five `[record:activity]` literals in the file. Four are authored-value channels (filterMode, unproduced types, non-array types, unrecognised types) and are now block-named. The fifth is the `sys_activity` row-type warning in `activityRowToFeedItem`.
- That fifth one is left unchanged on purpose. `activityRowToFeedItem` is exported from the package barrel and called by `@object-ui/app-shell` `RecordDetailView`, and two app-shell pins filter on that exact prefix. Changing it is an exported-signature change consumed outside plugin-detail, which this card's file surface excludes. The value it reports comes from `sys_activity` data, not from an author's block, so per-block dedupe does not apply to it. When it fires from `RecordDetailView`'s merged feed it still says `[record:activity]`; that is reported to the dispatching seat, not changed here.
- `record-chatter.tsx`'s old comment deferring this repair to this card is replaced by a description of the new behaviour.
